findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the leaf's --allow-model-change escape hatch with the parent's absolute 'refuses to start on model mismatch' invariant — either note in the leaf that this flag is a sanctioned refinement of parent invariant #2 (integrity preserved because model-change runs are undiffable), or update the parent to authorize the escape hatch.
evidence: Leaf: 'It refuses to start when the resolved id differs from the corpus baseline's provider_provenance.ran_model for that pass, unless --allow-model-change is passed, in which case the run is labelled model-change and can never be diffed against a baseline with a different id.'
Parent invariant #2: 'refuses to start when the configured model differs from the corpus baseline's provider_provenance.ran_model' — stated absolutely, with no escape hatch.
The escape hatch is integrity-preserving (model-change runs are undiffable), so it narrows rather than defeats the parity goal — hence incomplete_enumeration, not a contradiction.
findings.finding: The leaf introduces an --allow-model-change escape hatch (runs labelled 'model-change', undiffable against a differing baseline) that the parent epic's Model-parity invariant does not contain; the parent states an absolute 'refuses to start when the configured model differs from the corpus baseline's provider_provenance.ran_model'.
findings.location: Approach → Pinned targets ('unless --allow-model-change is passed'); parent 759e invariant #2 / AC 'refuses to run a pass on a model other than its production class'
scenarios: A reviewer checks the leaf against the parent contract and finds a flag the parent never authorized, unsure whether it is sanctioned scope.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether parity.py's caching check reuses the existing run-level cache telemetry (cache_diagnostics.cache_write_never_read / warn_if_cache_write_never_read, bug 1dbe) and the live positive-case pattern in tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py, or justify why a new predicate is needed rather than repackaging the existing one.

src/rebar/llm/cache_diagnostics.py:140 cache_write_never_read(records, min_calls=2) computes the exact across-a-run 'was the cache ever read' signal (docstring: 'every caching call paid the write PREMIUM and not one collected the read DISCOUNT')

findings.finding: The plan's 'caching check' (assert cache_read_tokens > 0 across a run's usage-log rows) reimplements prior art already in the repo: src/rebar/llm/cache_diagnostics.py provides run-level cache analysis (cache_write_never_read / warn_if_cache_write_never_read, bug 1dbe) over usage-log records, and tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py already asserts cache_read_tokens > 0 as the positive case. The plan does not mention reusing either.
scenarios: parity.py grows a second, independent cache-read predicate that can drift from cache_diagnostics.cache_write_never_read's semantics (e.g. min_calls, the write>0 gate, the 'first call is benign' rule)
The plan's 'on at least one call after the first' rule differs subtly from cache_write_never_read's 'caching call = wrote OR read nonzero' definition, so the two disagree on edge runs
findings.suggested_fix: Have the 'caching check' call rebar.llm.cache_diagnostics over the run's usage-log rows (reuse cache_write_never_read / a shared helper) rather than defining a fresh 'cache_read_tokens > 0 after the first call' rule in parity.py, so the eval harness and production cache diagnostics share one definition.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define caching-check behavior for empty/single-row usage logs (flag as uncached/incomplete rather than vacuously pass or error), and cover it in a unit fixture.
evidence: 'after each run, assert from the run's usage-log rows that cache_read_tokens > 0 on at least one call after the first'
No stated behavior for empty/single-row usage logs — 'at least one call after the first' presupposes >=2 calls
findings.finding: The caching assertion 'cache_read_tokens > 0 on at least one call after the first' is undefined when the usage-log has zero rows or only one row (e.g. the run errored early or made a single call) — such a run neither has cache reads nor is a legitimate 'cached' run, and the plan does not state whether it is flagged uncached or errors.
scenarios: A Tier-1 run that fails after one call produces a usage log with a single row; the caching assertion has no 'call after the first' to inspect and may pass vacuously, mislabel the run cached, or throw an unhandled error
